dedupe_keys.name: pynncml microwave link rainfall preparation and inference toolbox

description: PyNNcml converts commercial microwave-link observations into rainfall estimates and wet/dry classifications. Hai Victor Habi and Tel Aviv University’s Cellular Environmental Monitoring and Processing Lab publish a PyTorch toolbox with recurrent-network methods, baseline estimation, rainfall-field generation and interpolation. The repository includes a two-link example with a reference rain gauge and support for the OpenMRG dataset. Input geography, observation period and time step depend on the selected link measurements; the software does not supply a universal global rainfall record. Public Python code is free under MIT and PyPI currently lists version 0.3.7 for Python 3.9 or later. A limitation is that the supplied trained networks use a private training dataset, so that part of model preparation cannot be independently recreated from public inputs alone. Simulation uses include preparing rainfall forcing for urban drainage studies and comparing sensor-derived hazard observations. It relates to data-openmrg-microwave-links-radar-gauges-gothenburg as an explicitly supported source. Neither the package nor its trained models were installed, and rainfall accuracy, sampling compatibility and robustness claims were not tested.
